One BUG found: user-edited estimate number is overwritten by auto-generated number on the FIRST save of a new estimate (only issue). All other flows work: Settings tabs + URL params, Company Profile save to localStorage, Estimate Workbench expandable header editor (Client Info / Project Info / Pricing & Notes / Notes / Clarifications / Internal Notes), LiveSummary shows Markup + Contingency + Tax with correct % labels, new estimates load company profile defaults (markup, contingency, gst, estimator, quote validity → valid_until date auto-calculated, default_terms → clarifications), save persists full metadata (client_info, project_info, company_profile_snapshot, notes, clarifications, internal_notes, pricing_profile, markup_percent, contingency_percent, tax_rate, line_items), reload by ?id={uuid} restores everything except the estimate_number (due to the bug above).

ui_bugs.issue: User-edited estimate number is DISCARDED on the FIRST save of a new estimate. When !currentEstimateId (new estimate), the code unconditionally calls generateEstimateNumber() and overwrites any value the user typed into [data-testid='estimate-number-input']. Repro: create New Estimate → type 'EST-PHASE1-001' → Save → localStorage stores 'EST-2026-XXXX' instead. Per requirement 'Estimate Number (editable)' this must be preserved. Fix: only generate estNumber if !estimateNumber (i.e., estNumber = estimateNumber || generateEstimateNumber()).

critical_code_review_comments: EstimateWorkbench.jsx: `let estNumber = estimateNumber;` is immediately overwritten inside the if-block for new estimates, wasting the initial assignment and — more importantly — silently discarding the user's edit. Recommend: `estNumber = estimateNumber && estimateNumber.trim() ? estimateNumber : generateEstimateNumber();` (with a nullish/empty guard).

EstimateWorkbench.jsx line 62: COMPANY_PROFILE_KEY is duplicated in both EstimateWorkbench.jsx and CompanyProfile.jsx. Export a single constant from a shared module (or use the exported getCompanyProfile from CompanyProfile.jsx directly). Same for loadCompanyProfile function — duplication increases drift risk.
CompanyProfile.jsx: default_terms is a very long multiline template literal (bullet list). Fine, but consider extracting to a separate constants file for consistency with settings/branding.
CompanyProfile.jsx: no email/URL/phone validation on save — invalid emails or malformed websites silently persist. Add lightweight regex validation before saveCompanyProfile().
SettingsPage.jsx: importing CompanyProfile then rendering it inside a large monolithic 1092-line file — recommend continuing extraction (AccountTab.jsx, etc.) since file exceeds 700 lines threshold.

EstimateWorkbench.jsx: file is now 1179 lines — Phase 1 additions pushed it well past the 700-line guideline. Consider extracting <HeaderEditor/> (~320 lines of JSX) and <EstimateSelector/> dropdown into their own components.

EstimateWorkbench.jsx: `useEffect(..., [fetchLibraryData, fetchEstimates, searchParams, loadEstimate])` will re-run loadEstimate every time searchParams changes — a save-triggered setSearchParams({id}) will reset the just-loaded estimate. Verified working today but the dependency array is fragile.
LiveSummary.jsx duplicates the calculations useMemo from parent; pass `calculations` down as a prop to keep single source of truth (also flagged in iteration_31).
EstimateWorkbench.jsx uses browser confirm() in createNewEstimate + handleClearEstimate — carry-over from iteration_31.

rca of the issue: Estimate number persistence bug: EstimateWorkbench.jsx saveEstimate() at lines 310-319 initializes `estNumber = estimateNumber` then, inside `if (!estimateId)` (i.e., first save of a new estimate), unconditionally overrides `estNumber = generateEstimateNumber()`. Since the estimate_number input state is only bound to estimateNumber (which the user typed), that value is lost. Repro: 1) Open Estimate Workbench 2) Click Open → New Estimate 3) Type 'MY-CUSTOM-001' in [data-testid=estimate-number-input] 4) Add ≥1 line item 5) Click Save 6) localStorage.tradeos_estimates[0].estimate_number reads 'EST-YYYY-XXXX', not 'MY-CUSTOM-001'. Fix: `estNumber = (estimateNumber && estimateNumber.trim()) ? estimateNumber : generateEstimateNumber();`
